objects.name: Pronounce
objects.text: Pronunciation_____________     There are several things to know about pronunciation.  First, feel free to pronounce the words however you wish.  What follows is a short guide as to how the words are intended to be pronounced.  If a word just doesn't sound right to you and you like the way it looks, please, pronounce it how you will.     This guide is divided into three sections.  One section for consonants that appear at the beginning of a syllable, on for consonants that appear at the end of a syllable and one for vowels.     When generated the words will all be singular.  To pluralize a word simply add an 's' or and 'i' on the end to your satisfaction.Consonants at the beginning of syllablesb    backc    coldd    dof    fitg    givegr   greath    hithl   as hlackhr   as hrackj    justk    keptkh   as loch (Scottish)l    lowm    myn    nowp    potpl   as platept   as keptr    reads    seescl  as sclacksl   slopspr  sprawlst   staket    tenth   thoughttr   tripv    voicex    as visiony    yesz    zealVowelsa    bataa   as bat but longerae   wayai   as biteao   as owau   as aweay   waye    ebbé    flambéeh   as breathei   bitei    if unless at the word end then beeia   as mariaie   as beeio   polioiu   as eeuso    either over or oxoe   as noou   as youu    upû    urgey    denyConsonants at the end of syllablesb    cabch   as loch (Scottish)d    beddh   as bed and hewg    begh    as hewk    takel    alllr   tallerls   sellsm    himn    onncs  tanksnm   as enemyp    stopr    nearrr   rolled r (Spanish)s    misssch  as scotchsh   pusht    bitth   pathts   knotsv    live

objects.name: About
objects.text: Fantasy Language Creator 1.1____________________________This program is dedicated to Cosima Stiefer.Introduction     When I was young I, like many people, read and became fascinated by Tolkien's works.  As I got older I became interested in Role Playing Games.  The game I became the most involved with was RuneQuest™.  I created an elaborate world of my own, replete with maps, races, cultures and of course languages.     I created many words and names for things.  I have done some work on grammatical and syllabic structures.  Still, there are time when I tire of thinking up words for things and names for people and place.       To that end I have created, based solely upon the language I have created, a HyperCard program capable of generating words that follow the rules I have set upon my language.How it works     The program is quite simple.  It randomly generates a number of syllables, then it generates the type of syllable, and then the specific letters of each syllable.  It follows the structure of the language I have created and since the implementation works well most words are pronounceable.  There are times however that it will generate ludicrous or unpronounceable words.The program• Main Screen     There are four buttons on the Main Screen:     Begin - Takes you to the word generator.     About - Takes you to this screen.     Home - Takes you to your home stack.     Quit - Quits HyperCard.• Jaanaka     There are eleven buttons on this screen:     Six shadow box buttons:     New - When this button is clicked it will generate a single word of one to four syllables.  This gives greater control over the selection of words to be saved.     Batch - When this button is clicked it will ask you how many words you would like to generate.  The upper limit is probably in the vicinity of 32768.  It will warn you if you ask it to generate fifty or more words.  Note also that each time you generate a batch of words the field is cleared beforehand.     Save Word - This allows you to save words you have generated to the Lexicon.  If the batch list is full it will ask if that is what you wish to save.  If you do not wish to save the Batch List it will ask if you want to delete the contents of the Batch field and in any case will save the word in the Word field if one is present.     Print - This will print the Lexicon.     Sort/Export - When chosen this will give you the option to Sort the Lexicon, Export it, or both.  You may sort either alphabetical or reverse.     Main - This will take you back to the Main Screen.     One check box:     Longer Words - When this is checked the generator will generate longer words of three to six syllables.     Four radio buttons:     Lexicon - This will bring the Lexicon field forward.     Glossary - This will bring the Glossary field forward.     Pronunciation - This will bring the Pronunciation field forward.     Batch List - This will bring the Batch List field forward.     There are eight fields on this screen.     Number of Syllables - This small field just beneath the word Trade Tongue shows the number of syllables for the word being generated.     Type of Syllables - The next field shows the type of syllables being generated (i.e., CV, VC, etc.)  It progresses as the word generation does.     Word Generation - Then next field over is where the word itself appears.     Count - This field appears very near the words Jaanaka.  When you do a Batch generation this field counts down allowing you to have an idea of how much longer it is going to take.     Lexicon - This field and the ones below are in the same location on the screen.  They are the largest fields on the screen as well.  Lexicon holds the words that you have decided to save.  It is editable and you may make notes of define the words you have saved.     Glossary - This field is not editable.  It contains a smattering of the words I have created over the years as well as some that I have generated with this program.     Pronunciation - This is not able to be edited either.  This contains information on the correct pronunciation of the words as well as some information about the syllabic structure.     Batch - This contains the words that were generated by the Batch command.  This is editable as well allowing you to correct the words to your liking before saving them to the Lexicon.• About FLC     This screen.
